DE.name: Wermut
DE.citation: ScienceDirect topic overview; also documented as Wermutkraut, Bitterer Beifuss. Distinguished from Artemisia abrotanum (Eberraute/southernwood), a related but distinct European medicinal species

FR.name: Absinthe
FR.citation: ScienceDirect topic overview; also documented as Armoise amere, Herbe aux vers, Herbe d'absinthe. The species from which the alcoholic beverage absinthe takes its name

GB.name: Wormwood
GB.citation: Britannica; native to Europe. Also documented as green ginger, grand wormwood, madderwort. Distinguished from the unrelated Artemisia annua (source of the antimalarial artemisinin), Artemisia maritima (sea wormwood) and Artemisia alba (white wormwood)

RU.name: Полынь горькая
RU.citation: Russian Wikipedia (formal citation: Gubanov et al., Illustrated Key to Plants of Central Russia); Moscow State University herbarium database (plant.depo.msu.ru); Plantarium.ru. Considered the bitterest plant in the Russian flora

US.name: Common wormwood
US.citation: Britannica; naturalized from Europe, found in fields and roadsides (Flora of the Southeastern United States). Historically used as an anthelmintic (anti-parasitic); key ingredient in absinthe and vermouth. SAFETY: contains thujone, toxic at elevated levels
